questions.question: Does the new pan outlet line up with the soil pipe?

rules.rationale: Merchants split fittings by joint technology, so the kit carries one family only.
Merchants split fittings by joint technology, so the kit carries one family only.
Merchants split fittings by joint technology, so the kit carries one family only.

A wall-hung WC needs a concealed frame, a flush plate and a wall-hung pan. The frames cited ship a 90 mm bend with a 90/110 mm adaptor, so a separate 110 mm pan connector is not added (this differs from the original brief). Plate must match the cistern maker and series; that compatibility is a SKU check, not encoded here.
A close-coupled WC needs a pan of the chosen height, its cistern, seat, flush lever and an isolating valve; no frame.
A back-to-wall WC needs its pan, a concealed cistern with a flush button, a unit or boxing to hide it, a seat and an isolating valve; no frame.
Mira guides warn stud partitions may need alternative fixings; wall fixings are not supplied.
Wall fixings suited to the substrate are not supplied.
The connector depends on the soil position: horizontal outlet to P trap.
The connector depends on the soil position: S or turned P trap.
Wall-hung frames connect through their own 90/110 mm adaptor whatever the soil position.
Pan installation needs packers, silicone and PTFE.
A back-to-wall pan is floor-fixed like a close-coupled pan: packers, silicone and PTFE.
Where the outlet is offset or its position is not known, a flexible connector replaces the rigid one.
A standard-height close-coupled WC uses the standard pan.
A comfort-height close-coupled WC uses the comfort-height pan.

finish_levels.label: Budget
finish_levels.description: The cheapest option that still meets the rules, where the research found one. Lines without a budget option keep the standard pick.

finish_levels.label: Standard
finish_levels.description: The option the research found most used, and compliant. This is the default; it is labelled 'most used' only where the evidence grade is B or better.

finish_levels.label: Premium
finish_levels.description: A higher-specification option where the research found one. Never pre-selected; paid add-ons stay off even at this level.

schema_changes: job-kit-ui/2 is additive over job-kit-ui/1: every v1 field keeps its name and meaning.
Top level: finish_levels [{id, label, description}] and schema_changes [string].
Question: help, widget (cards|segmented|toggle|select), reason_upfront, unknown {label, maps_to} (answer "unknown" resolves to maps_to) and impact (equal to priority).
Line option: evidence_grade (A-D), why_default and price_band {min, max, currency, per, vat, observed_on, basis} (prices are dated observations, not quotes).
Line: forced_by {text, source_url} (a rule fixes this line; explain it, do not offer a choice) and help.
finish_level selects on every line with options the option tagged with that level if present (the line default when it carries the tag), otherwise the line default.
